home.title: One team setup for every DSH.
home.tagline: Publish models, presets and plugin pins once; every member's DeepSeek Harness picks them up.
home.eyebrow: The team edition of DeepSeek Harness
home.lede: Publish models, presets and plugin pins once, and every member's DeepSeek Harness picks them up. Team-model calls go through the platform's gateway, so provider keys never leave the server.
home.hint: Already on DSH? Type /teamwork login in your terminal.

surface.label: Surface · where you already work
surface.title: Keep your tools. Sync once, and the team's setup is there.
surface.lede: Members keep their own DSH. The team's models and presets appear next to their own configuration, and nothing of theirs is overwritten.
surface.step1Body: Add team models, presets and plugin pins in the team console, and invite members with single-use links.
surface.step2Title: Members sign in to the team
surface.step2Body: Run /teamwork login in DSH and confirm on the website. DSH finishes signing in by itself.
surface.step3Body: Run /teamwork sync, or let it run itself: once after sign-in, then every minute. The team's models and presets are then in DSH, and calls to team models go through the gateway.
surface.termSynced: Synced: 2 team models, 1 preset, 1 plugin pin
surface.termNoKey: No provider key stored on this machine

boundary.label: Boundary · safe to hand over
boundary.title: The keys stay on the server. Membership is checked on every request.
boundary.lede: No API keys pasted into a chat, and no rotating them when someone leaves. The team gets a path the platform guards.
boundary.keysBody: Provider keys live only in the server's environment. A member's DSH holds a team token, which cannot call a provider by itself.
boundary.checkBody: Every request re-reads the caller's membership. Remove someone, and their next request is refused.
boundary.gatewayBody: The gateway forwards an allow-list of inference fields, and none of the provider's headers come back.
boundary.promise: Nothing a caller sends can name a URL, a header or a key.
boundary.promiseNote: The model is resolved within your team; the provider and its key are the server's to choose.

deep.label: Deep · what the team shares
deep.title: Publish once. Everyone runs the same thing.
deep.lede: A team setup is three kinds of thing. Presets sit on top: each uses a team model and pins the plugins it needs. Change one once, and every member's next sync carries it.
deep.presetsBody: The team's prompt, tool requirements and plugin pins, on a team model or a model of its own.
deep.pluginsBody: npm packages at exact versions, so everyone runs the same build. Installing one stays each member's choice.
deep.modelsBody: A provider and a model the platform calls for the team, with the key on the server.

community.label: Community edition · run it yourself
community.title: Or run it on your own server.
community.lede: What one team needs is open source under Apache-2.0: teams, models, presets, plugin pins and the gateway. It runs as Postgres and one Node container from compose.yaml, and provider keys stay in your own server's environment.

faq.label: Questions
faq.title: Before you start
faq.q1: Where do the provider keys live?
faq.a1: Only in the DSH Teamwork server's environment. A member's DSH holds a team token that lasts 30 days; team-model calls are forwarded by the server, and the token cannot reach a provider directly.
faq.q2: Do we have to change DSH?
faq.a2: No. Install the @dsh-teamwork/dsh-teamwork plugin, run /teamwork login, and /teamwork sync pulls the team's setup (it also syncs on its own every minute). The team's setup sits next to each member's own and overwrites nothing.
faq.a3: No. Conversations stay in each member's DSH. The platform forwards team-model calls to the provider and does not store them.
faq.q4: What happens when we remove a member?
faq.a4: Their next request is refused. Membership is checked on every request, so there is no waiting for a token to expire.
faq.q5: Can one person be in several teams?
faq.a5: Not yet: one person belongs to one team.

final.label: Start
final.title: Set up your team and publish its first model.
final.lede: Sign in, create a team, publish a team model. Once members sync, their first call goes through the gateway.
